articles.title: Box Office: ‘Avengers: Endgame Encore’ Returns to No. 1 With $26 Million, ‘Primetime’ Scores Impressive $19 Million Debut
articles.summary: “Avengers: Endgame Encore,” a re-release of Disney and Marvel’s 2019 blockbuster (with extra footage!), emerged victorious at the domestic box office over several new releases.
body: “Avengers: Endgame Encore” generated $26 million from 3,060 North American theaters over the weekend, a sizable haul for a movie that’s been available to watch online for years. It was even bigger overseas with $60 million for a massive global tally of $86 million. Excitement for the re-release certainly bodes well for the studio’s upcoming “Avengers: Doomsday,” which opens in December and brings back nearly all of Earth’s Mightiest Heroes on another save-the-planet mission.

Among new releases, A24’s “ Primetime ” enjoyed a sizable $19.2 million debut from 2,863 venues. This marks the third-best opening ever for A24, ranking behind this summer’s juggernaut “Backrooms” ($81.4 million) and Alex Garland’s 2024 dystopian “Civil War” ($25.5 million) and ahead of Josh Safdie and Timothée Chalamet’s 2025 frenetic sports drama “Marty Supreme” ($15.7 million). “Primetime,” directed by Lance Oppenheim and starring Robert Pattinson as “To Catch a Predator” host Chris Hansen, was produced for just $15 million, so it’s already well-positioned to turn a theatrical profit.

articles.title: ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ Sets Sights on Best Picture Oscar Nomination: ‘If the Possibility Is Not Zero, It’s Hard Not to Have a Little Bit of Hope’
articles.summary: “Godzilla Minus One” made franchise history in 2024 when it won Best Visual Effects at the 96th Academy Awards, becoming the first Godzilla film to win an Oscar. Now, after Takashi Yamazaki’s highly anticipated sequel, “Godzilla Minus Zero,” premiered to rave reviews at the New York Film Festival…
body: The VFX Oscar win for 2023’s “Godzilla Minus One” was an unlikely feat in itself. On a budget of just $15 million, Yamazaki assembled a visual effects team of just 35 artists to create 610 effects shots. The underdog film clinched the win against a lineup of Hollywood goliaths, including Disney’s “Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3,” Paramount’s “Mission: Impossible — Dead Reckoning Part One” and Apple’s “Napoleon.” The historic nomination also made Yamazaki (who began his career in visual effects) the first feature director recognized in the visual effects category since Stanley Kubrick for “2001: A Space Odyssey.”

“It’s going to take me a few years to process what has happened and what it all means,” Yamazaki told Variety on the awards circuit in 2023. “But I have to thank Godzilla for opening the door and paving the way and making it to the Oscars.”

articles.title: ‘A joyful place’: a new museum coaxes Austrians to embrace The Sound of Music
articles.summary: Sixty years after the film’s release, Salzburg is embracing a Hollywood classic it once kept at arm’s length. Let’s start at the very beginning – famously, a very good place to start.
body: Just two decades after the second world war, a Hollywood crew descended on Salzburg with stars, show tunes and a compelling, essentially true story of love and opposition to Adolf Hitler: The Sound of Music.
The Austrian city, still economically and morally devastated from the Nazi period, wasn’t quite ready to receive them.

Although director Robert Wise was free to make use of the glorious Alpine settings and the old town’s historical facades, scenes such as soldiers marching across the central Residenzplatz under swastika flags made municipal authorities deeply uneasy.
When the film premiered in 1965, it ran for a couple of weeks, closed for lack of ticket sales and largely disappeared from local memory. That is until the tour buses started coming.

articles.title: NAZA film-makers address threats at documentary’s New York City premiere
articles.summary: Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor defend findings on Israel’s killing of Palestinians amid threats from Israeli officials. The film-makers behind NAZA, the award-winning documentary on Israel’s systemic mass killing of Palestinians in Gaza, defended their findings at the film’s North American premiere…
body: The critically acclaimed film, directed by Oscar-winning film-makers Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor and produced by the Guardian, features the testimony of 24 anonymized Israeli soldiers and intelligence officers involved in the surveillance and remote killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza, who describe the AI-powered systems used to select their targets. The project takes its name from an acronym used euphemistically by Israeli intelligence to indicate how many civilians it expects to die in an airstrike, which are often conducted at night in private homes, killing many family members, including children, at once.

“Our country is doing so much to hide these systems,” Szor told the audience at the New York film festival in a Q&A that followed the film’s premiere. “It’s not a world that is open even to the Israeli public.”
“These crimes that you saw are ongoing,” Abraham said. “They’re ongoing because it’s what our country is doing, and because of what your country is supporting and funding.”

articles.title: Anna Kendrick Is “Over the Moon” About Directing ‘The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo’
articles.summary: The 'Babies' actress covered George Clooney, 'Twilight' ("what the f*** am I doing here?") and 'Pitch Perfect's "revisionist history" in a career-spanning conversation at the Zurich Film Festival.
body: Anna Kendrick was in fine form Sunday afternoon as the U.S. star continues to traverse the festival circuit with Babies.

At a Zurich Film Festival masterclass session, Kendrick took an adoring crowd through the early years of her career all the way to an Oscar nomination for Up in the Air, as well as stories from her time on Pitch Perfect, A Simple Favor, and her directorial debut, 2023’s Woman of the Hour.

Kendrick found herself taking the character where she wanted to go instead of what the casting director was imagining. “If I’d known there was a real interest in me, I would have absolutely bungled the read,” she said about trying for the role of the ambitious, no-nonsense Natalie in the comedy-drama. “Because I just thought, ‘Obviously, they’re gonna hire someone incredibly classy.’ I went in and did an awkward, goofy read, and that’s what got me the job because nobody else did the audition that way,” she said.

articles.title: Leonard Nimoy Worked On A '90s Sci-Fi Series That's Never Mentioned
articles.summary: Despite having a creative premise, big-name guest stars, and a pilot episode directed by Leonard Nimoy, this '90s sci-fi series was short-lived.
body: It's okay if you don't remember the UPN series "Deadly Games." Few probably do. The UPN, as some may recall, debuted in January 1995 along with the pilot episode of "Star Trek: Voyager." Paramount had long been interested in the TV game and had even considered launching its own TV network centered on a "Star Trek" series as far back as 1978. It finally got its wish nearly two decades later, although much of the UPN's original programming wasn't terribly popular.

"Deadly Games" was one of the network's early short-lived attempts at a successful sci-fi show. It wasn't a success, sadly, premiering in September 1995 and lasting only 13 episodes before ending the following January. In a surprising piece of talent wrangling, however, Leonard Nimoy served as an executive producer and directed the show's pilot episode, "Killshot."

articles.title: John Turturro on Joining the Oscar Race — and ‘Severance’ Season 3
articles.summary: The Zurich Golden Eye winner sat down for a masterclass session in Switzerland, where he spoke about the long-overdue buzz for his latest performance in 'The Only Living Pickpocket in New York.'
body: Hot on the heels of his Golden Eye award ceremony on Saturday night, John Turturro entertained another crowd at a Zurich Film Festival masterclass on Sunday.

In a career-spanning conversation with Deadline ‘s Melanie Goodfellow — the actor’s shining Golden Eye trophy neatly nestled between them — Turturro discussed growing up in an immigrant household, his decades-long friendship with Spike Lee, and the transition from acting to filmmaking.

Turturro, who has steadily become one of the industry’s most formidable actors yet to put “Oscar nominee” on his resume, was asked about joining the best actor race this year with the Sundance success The Only Living Pickpocket in New York. “I never really have gone the whole hog with it,” he responded about the upcoming awards campaign. “But now I’m the lead in the film, so I’m going to support the film because I love the film.”

articles.title: 5 Action Thrillers From The 2020s That Are Destined To Be Future Classics
articles.summary: From international releases to home-grown affairs, here are five action thrillers released in the 2020s that will become classics (if they aren't already).
body: There are few genres that can inspire the sort of loyalty that action movies do. Perhaps rivaled only by horror, action movie die-hards are always on the hunt for the next great thing. But what do the best action movies ever have in common? What takes something from good to great? What helps a great movie become an eventual classic? Those are questions worth asking when looking at some of the best the genre has to offer over the last handful of years.

The 2020s have been nothing if not interesting for the movie business, which has been entirely reshaped by the pandemic, streaming, and other elements in the ever-changing landscape. But the streaming era has given us some truly great action flicks, such as "Extraction" and "Triple Frontier." Imports from around the world have gotten more screen time in North America. In many ways, it's a great time for action cinema.
